value: Published continuous torque is the cap from zero to the published rated speed; zero supported torque above that speed. Known lower mechanical maximum further restricts speed. This assumes suitable FOC control and adequate stated thermal mounting, and does not invent stall torque or a mechanical speed limit.
Every included motor uses the same rated_continuous envelope, including maxon variants with fuller stall data.
Published peaks are preserved but do not improve continuous load capacity; unknown duration remains blank.

Use source motor mass. Frameless rotor/stator sets are assumed integrated into the already modeled frame. Unmodeled custom motor housings, support bearings, encoders, wiring and controls receive no invented mass allowance; the result is a conceptual assembled-stock study rather than a complete manufactured-arm mass prediction.
Conservative cylindrical body envelope; known complete axial lengths >=100 mm are excluded. Unknown shaft/cable envelopes remain identified in provenance.
Published upper-bound weights are used as conservative mass values, with their bound qualifier retained here.
Continuous cap is min(published rated output torque at 2000 rpm, published average output torque limit). No peak torque is treated as continuous.
Evaluation input speed capped at min(published mechanical maximum, average input speed limit if published, 2000 rpm). This avoids extrapolating the torque rating beyond its published reference speed.
Remains null and is not an extra evaluated constraint. Published output torque limits and input speed limits are still enforced; input-shaft strength is not certified.
Published inertia has no explicit shaft-reference declaration in the researched source, so it is not silently assigned to a rotating shaft. Rotor inertia uses published motor values.
Any variant with a contradictory official website/PDF field is excluded, including conflicts limited to a peak or an envelope value.
Only SKU-backed public-store reducer ratios are included. Procurement stock is not asserted. PDF-only and selector-only variants are not input candidates.
Original approved base geometry, local assembly fit checks and derived stock masses remain authoritative. Global travel collisions and joint stops remain disabled as previously requested.
